items.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: waiting until you hear Tony Hatch come in and say, “Okay one, two, three,”

ctx.x: The string section is in front of me in the studio and the violins, the cellos, and so on, facing me. And here I am with my music stand facing them. Next to me was another guitarist, I can’t think of who was on that session, and I was playing a twelve string. I borrowed Les’ twelve string guitar for that because I didn’t have one. And I’m looking at the music, I’m turning the pages, all the string section, they’re all reading the New York Times, reading the newspapers, waiting until you hear Tony Hatch come in…
And then just from the experience of the strings, what a chill down my spine listening to them right in front of you. It was a first experience with the strings, oh fabulous.
